newsitem.title: CHINA: Northwest China earthquake leaves 14 injured.
newsitem.headline: Northwest China earthquake leaves 14 injured.

text.p: At least 14 people were injured and hundreds of buildings were destroyed when two large earthquakes just five hours apart rocked China's northwestern Xinjiang region on Sunday, local officials said.
"It felt very strong," an official of the Jiashi Seismological Bureau said by telephone. "The ground seemed to move from left to right for about one minute."
The first earthquake measuring 6.3 on the open-ended Richter scale struck the town of Jiashi at 7.46 a.m. on Sunday (2346 GMT Saturday), the official said.
That was followed by a stronger tremor of magnitude 6.4 that jolted the region at 12.36 p.m. (0436 GMT), he said.
At least 14 people were injured, including five who were seriously hurt, and thousands of buildings were destroyed after the two earthquakes, the official Xinhua news agency said.
State radio said about 3,000 buildings, mainly houses, collapsed and some 100 head of livestock were killed in Jiashi, a region populated mainly by sheep herders and cotton farmers.
However, no deaths were expected in Jiashi because most residents have been living in tents since an earthquake measuring 6.4 struck the town in January, killing 50 people, he said.
"People had been warned not to return to their houses yet so we don't think there will be many casualties, and probably no deaths," the Jiashi Seismological Burea official said.
"We have had warnings of more earthquakes," he said. "But the earthquakes today felt much stronger than the one last January."
The Jiashi district has been hit by hundreds of aftershocks since January as well as several other earthquakes that have caused widespread damage.
On March 20, an earthquake measuring 6.9 hit Jiashi, killing 24 people and injuring 40. That came just days after a tremor of 6.0 magnitude left two people dead and injured three.
Many of the region's residents live in earthen houses that are easily damaged by earthquakes, and relief teams were searching through the rubble for casualties and survivors, the official said.
However, this was the first time that a series of earthquakes had occurred in Xinjiang, state radio said.
More tremors were expected in the region, it said, quoting seismological experts.
